#744. Joan Smalls Says Tom Brady Was "Catalyst" for Candice Swanepoel Feud

Joan Smalls addressed her and fellow Victoria's Secret Angel Candice Swanepoel's friendship fallout, confirming that the South African model's new romance with Tom Brady was the reason.

Joan Smalls is strutting away from relationships that don't respect girl code.

One month after rumors emerged that the Victoria's Secret supermodel was unhappy with fellow runway star Candice Swanepoel for dating her former fling Tom Brady, she confirmed the New England Patriots alum was at the center of their friendship breakup.

"Unfortunately, that was the catalyst," Smalls said during the Nov. 25 episode of The Cutting Room Floor podcast. "I was seeing this person for a period of eight months."

E! News has reached out to reps for Swanepoel and Brady for comment and has not yet heard back.

Though Smalls doesn't consider Brady to be an ex, she clarified that they casually dated the former NFL star on and off between 2023 and 2024. Swanepoel went on to spark romance rumors with Brady in June.

And for her part, Smalls emphasized that before ending her and Swanepoel's 15-year friendship—which she confirmed took place in April—they were each other's confidants about love and heartbreak.

"You've seen the relationships, situationships and people I've dated, and I've confided in you in these spaces and we never had a crossover," she reflected. "All of a sudden, I stopped seeing this person, and three months later, you text me and say, 'Oh, we have to speak about something,' which is usually not a conversation we normally have."

The Puerto Rican-born model—who had confirmed their fallout in scathing comments under her own Instagram posts last month—had a feeling that Swanepoel, 38, was planning to name him her MVP.

"I called her and I asked her, I said, 'Is this about him?' She said, 'Yes,'" she recalled. "We spoke on the phone very briefly, and I was just perplexed and lost for words."

The confrontation was especially devastating because Smalls said Swanepoel—who was previously linked to model Andrés Velencoso in 2022—had been a guiding light during her romance with the Fox Sports commentator.

"She helped me write text messages to this person," Smalls, also 38, said. "She knew intimate things. Potentially to my detriment, I overshared. I was just being open with a friend that I thought was a safe spac

As for how the conversation went? Smalls accused her former friend of committing a cardinal girl code sin: Dating a guy your friend was romantically involved with.

"She came across as justifying her actions," she explained. "She started diminishing my experience to make herself feel better about the situation, which I think is what infuriated me."

Smalls believed that Swanepoel—who shares two sons with ex Hermann Nicoli—refused to take accountability for being a bad friend.

"It was this whole attitude of 'I'm an adult. I don't need permission,'" she posited. "Both are actually true: you are an adult and you don't need permission. But as a friend, you should consider me in your choices. Don't consider me in your apologies."

"Then she was like, 'Well, I'm sorry, but I'm going to explore this and so is life,'" she continued. "It was just this attitude of entitlement and lack of care towards someone who's your friend and something that I would never do to you."

Looking back at the conversation, Smalls felt that Swanepoel was looking to ease her own mind.

As she put it, "She wanted me to comfort her about her bad decision so that she didn't feel guilty by her choice and then she would constantly justify it."

It was especially difficult for the model since she prefers to keep her inner circle small.

"I rarely allow people into my life, and I'm very private," Smalls added. "So, if I let you into a space that I thought you would protect me as my friend, that's the only one thing I asked for you to do. Create a safe space for me to be myself, to open up, and you can't do that."

Following initial speculations about their fallout, Swanepoel's team detailed her perspective on their friendship.

"Candice has always been exceptionally private about her personal life, with her focus remaining on raising her children," her rep Amanda Ruisi told E! News in October. "She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect."

As Smalls and Swanepoel navigate life after their friendship, keep reading for more famous celebrity feuds.

The Sex and the City costars had dodged feud rumors for years, but they were reignited after Cattrall decided not to return for a third movie and made comments about her SLP that raised eyebrows.

"What was your reaction to Kim Cattrall telling Piers Morgan that you were never friends just colleagues?" Andy Cohen asked Parker on a September 2017 episode of Watch What Happens Live.

As she explained, "Just...heartbroken. I mean that whole week, you and I spoke about it because I was just...I don't know I found it really upsetting because that's, you know, that's not the way I recall our experience."

"So...it's sad but I'm kind of...I don't know, I always think that what ties us together is this singular experience is the thing," she continued. "It was a professional experience but it became personal because it was years and years of our lives. So I'm hoping that that sort of eclipses anything that's been recently spoken. That many years spent doing something so special that people had a connection with is such a privileged."

And though they didn't film scenes together, Cattrall did make a small appearance on And Just Like That.

During a 2022 TikTok challenge, JoJo Siwa described Candace Cameron Bure as the "rudest" celebrity, later explaining that she felt snubbed when Bure once refused to take a picture with her on a red carpet. Shortly after the dig, however, the Full House alum apologized: "I kind of broke your 11-year-old heart. I didn't take a picture with you. Ugh! I feel crummy, I feel—JoJo, I'm so sorry."

The two made amends. But months later, Cameron Bure was asked if she expects the Great American Family network, of which she serves as chief creative officer, to feature same-sex couples as leads in holiday movies. She said no, adding, "I think that Great American Family will keep traditional marriage at the core."

Siwa, who came out as a member of the LGBTQ+ community in 2021, wrote on Instagram that the actress' comment is "rude and hurtful to a whole community of people."

In August 2022, Morris and Pope traded harsh words with Aldean, wife of fellow country star Jason Aldean, after she shared an Instagram Reel of herself applying makeup, writing, "I'd really like to thank my parents for not changing my gender when I went through my tomboy phase. I love this girly life."

Berk (pictured second from left) addressed rumors of a falling out with France (middle) in January 2024, two months after he announced his exit from Queer Eye after eight seasons.

"I want people to know that Tan and I—we will be fine," he told Vanity Fair. "There was a situation, and that's between Tan and I, and it has nothing to do with the show. It was something personal that had been brewing—and nothing romantic, just to clarify that."

In March 2024, France responded to allegations that he had campaigned to replace Berk on Queer Eye with his friend Jeremiah Brent.

"Netflix and the production companies did a full-on casting. I didn't put my friend up for the job. They ended up getting it because they were the best person for the job," he said on Instagram. "But I didn't get them hired by getting rid of somebody else."

In September 2023, while playing a game called Stir the Pot with her daughter Kelly Osbourne on E! News, Sharon said the That '70s Show alum was the rudest celebrity she had ever met, branding him, a "rude, rude, rude, rude little boy" and a "dastardly little thing."

He did not respond to her remarks publicly.

Five years prior, Sharon told Larry King that when Ashton appeared on The Talk in 2014, he had an "attitude" after she got his name wrong.

"He goes, 'What are you, what have you done in this industry?'" she recalled. "And I was like, 'Kid, don't start with me, because I'm gonna eat you up and s--t you out.' So I was just like, 'You don't know what you're dealing with, kid.'"

Back in June 2021, the Hole frontwoman accused Rodrigo of copying her band's album cover for a promotional photo without giving credit, prompting the Disney alum to respond, "Love u and live through this sooooo much."

however, it seemed their hatchet was buried when Love replied, "Olivia - you're welcome. My favorite florist is in Notting Hill, London! Dm me for deets! I look forward to reading your note [winking face emoji]."

During a 2019 appearance on Watch What Happens Live, the Happy Days actor was asked why he didn't get along with the Forrest Gump star on the set of the 1989 flick Turner & Hooch.

"I was directing that movie for 13 days," Winkler recalled, "and then I was called into [producer] Jeff Katzenberg's office and he said, 'You have everything with you? Go home.'"

He did, however, seem to get along with Hanks' four-legged costar, quipping, "Love that dog."

Winkler later denied speculation that he still had beef with the Oscar winner, telling TMZ in 2020, "I don't have a feud with Tom Hanks."

Fans of The Hills will remember that iconic line, delivered by Conrad on the season three premiere. Their feud began when Montag started dating her now-husband Spencer Pratt, and hit its peak when Conrad accused her and Pratt of starting a rumor that she had made a sex tape with then-boyfriend Jason Wahler.

The costars reignited their ongoing feud in 2017 when Gibson publicly called out Johnson on Instagram after the Fast and Furious 9 release date was pushed back to April 2020. That same day, it was announced that a Fast and Furious spinoff starring Johnson and Jason Statham would hit theaters in 2019. The following month, Gibson threatened to quit Fast 9 if Johnson was in the movie.

Gibson then opened up about the feud, telling Van Lathan on The Red Pill podcast, "I have yet to talk to The Rock to this day, and we will have a conversation." He shared that he did have a chat with the former wrestler's producing partner, but not the actor himself.

"I found myself being the messenger on behalf of various people associated to the franchise, but stupid me was the only one who went public about those feelings, which is my own fault," gibson said. "It's not professional, it's not cool."

Swift and Perry had been in a feud for years, with their rift even allegedly inspiring the former's song "Bad Blood." The drama, which reportedly started over a backup dancer and competing tours, came to an end after Perry sent Swift a literal olive branch before her Reputation Tour kickoff in 2018.

"So I just got to my dressing room and found this actual olive branch," Swift said in an Instagram video. "This mean so much."

She captioned the video, "Thank you Katy."

The iconic singers have been feuding since 2004. While accepting the Classic Songwriter Award at the Q Awards that year, John said to attendees, "Madonna, best f--king live act? F--k off! Since when has lip-syncing been live? Sorry about that, but I think everyone who lip-syncs in public on stage, when you pay like 75 quid to see them, should be shot."

The former Grey's Anatomy star sparked a feud with the series creator in 2008 when she removed her name from the Emmy Awards consideration. Heigl stated that her reason for the move was because she wasn't "given the material to warrant a nomination."

Rhimes later opened up about Heigl's decision during an interview with Oprah Winfrey on Oprah's Next Chapter in 2012. "On some level it stung and on some level I was not surprised," she said. "When people show you who they are, believe them. I carry that [mantra] with me a lot. It has served me well."

It was the New York Fashion Week fight heard 'round the world when Nicki and Cardi got into a heated altercation at the Harper's Bazaar Icon party. The following month, Cardi opened up about the catalyst for the fight with Nicki.

"For a while now she's been taking a lot of shots at me," Cardi said in W magazine's Art Issue. "I spoke to her twice before, and we came to an understanding. But she kept it going."

The real spark of the fight came when Cardi saw that Nicki had allegedly liked and then unliked a tweet about Cardi's parenting skills, which Nicki has denied.

"I was going to make millions off my Bruno Mars tour, and I sacrificed that to stay with my daughter," Cardi continued. "I love my daughter. I'm a good-ass f--king mom. So for somebody that don't have a child to like that comment? So many people want to say that party wasn't the time or the place, but I'm not going to catch another artist in the grocery store or down the block."

Tension between Kanye and Taylor first started in 2009, when the "Stronger" rapper took the stage during her acceptance speech at the MTV Video Music Awards. Years later, the two would make up and even become friends, but that came to an end in 2016 after the release of his song "Famous," in which he name-checks the "End Game" singer.

In February 2025, one day before the Grammys, Kanye updated his Instagram to follow only Taylor. He added no further comment, and his fellow musician did not respond publicly to the move.

Carey and J.Lo's supposed feud started when the Queen of Christmas was asked to give her opinion on several singers during a 2003 German TV interview. When asked her opinion on Lopez, she replied, "I don't know her."

#743. 'Best midfielder in the world' - where does Bellingham rank?

Bellingham finished 11th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or

Is there a better central midfielder on the planet than Jude Bellingham right now?

Not according to Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid manager might be trying to manage the Englishman's minutes, but he did not hold back in his praise after the 23-year-old came off the bench and scored a superb volley, helping Real overturn a half-time deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

"He has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything," Mourinho said.

"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world."

Bellingham's impressive 45-minute cameo came just nine days after an outstanding, all-action display for England in a 3-2 Nations League win in Spain.

'Extravagant, brilliant!' - Bellingham's wonder goal

While the former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund player also earned plenty of plaudits for his displays at the 2026 World Cup, where he scored seven times, Mourinho believes Bellingham's unique blend of craft and graft isn't yet fully appreciated.

"He can play as a '10', as an '8', with two pivots, with one," Mourinho said after the win against PSV. "That's why I said, when the Ballon d'Or was discussed, that it was outrageous he wasn't among the top 10."

While wingers like Lamine Yamal or Michael Olise are also likely to be contenders for the 2027 award, is there anyone you would rather have in central midfield than Bellingham?

BBC Sport looks at what makes him so good, and who his closest challengers are.

Although only 23, Bellingham is already in his fourth year at Real Madrid and is on course for his most productive campaign since his debut season in 2023-24, when he scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists, including setting up Vinicius Jr in the Champions League final.

He has seven goals and four assists in 18 appearances this season. Only three central midfielders have more goal involvements across Europe's top five leagues, but Bellingham's all-round game is what sets him apart.

He leads his Real team-mates for possession won, duels won and fouls won. And while only Kylian Mbappe has had more shots on target, Bellingham offers far more than just late runs into the box.

He has played more passes into the final third than any other Real player, leads the club for ball carries and is second only to Arda Guler for chances created.

When Bellingham's coaches at Birmingham gave him the number 22 shirt, it reflected their belief that he could play any role, as a number 10, 8 or 4.

He has fulfilled that potential to become the complete midfielder.

While Bellingham made his senior debut with Birmingham, Vitinha also spent part of his formative years in the Midlands, scoring once in 22 appearances during a loan spell at Wolves - a spectacular long-range strike against Chorley in 2021.

But goalscoring isn't what the Portuguese playmaker is best known for - it is his metronomic passing.

The 26-year-old has played a pivotal role in Paris St-Germain's back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with manager Luis Enrique saying he "embodies the perfect midfielder".

He was named man of the match in the victory over Arsenal last season, having completed 141 of his 150 passes, matching the Champions League final record set by Barcelona's Xavi in 2011.

Vitinha finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting in 2025 but slipped to 14th this year, a ranking Luis Enrique disagreed with.

"It's a real pleasure to have a player with such physical abilities and that mentality," the PSG boss said last month. "He's at an incredible level."

Rice finished one place below Vitinha, and four below England team-mate Bellingham, in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings after helping Arsenal win their first Premier League title since 2004.

He briefly played at centre-back as a youngster at West Ham before establishing himself as a top-class defensive midfielder for the Hammers. But since joining the Gunners in 2023 he has taken his game to another level, adding significantly more attacking output.

Rice created 17 big chances in the Premier League last season, as defined by Opta, a total bettered only by Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki.

The 27-year-old has also registered 14 assists in all club competitions since August 2025. While set-pieces have undoubtedly contributed to that tally, he offers much more.

He ranks among the top 4% of central midfielders across Europe's top five leagues for progressive carries, while posting similarly impressive figures for chances created, touches and expected assists.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner missed Spain's Nations League defeat by England this month through injury, and his absence was keenly felt as the hosts uncharacteristically struggled for control, at least against 11 men.

It was a far cry from Spain's triumphant Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup campaigns, both of which ended with him being named player of the tournament.

The 30-year-old completed 756 passes as Spain won their second global title, the highest total ever recorded at a World Cup.

His performances this summer were all the more impressive given that he had taken time to return to his best after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament, an injury that sidelined him for most of the 2024-25 campaign.

The former Manchester City player has slotted in seamlessly since joining Barcelona in August, and averages 106 successful passes per 90 minutes in La Liga - the second-highest figure, behind Vitinha, of any player in the top five European leagues.

The student playing in La Liga: Introvert Rodri's unique rise to top

Pedri may be six years younger than Rodri, his midfield partner at the Camp Nou, but he boasts extraordinary experience for a 24-year-old, having made more than 250 appearances for Barcelona, not to mention playing at two European Championships and two World Cups.

The Tenerife-born midfielder combines tigerish work-rate with quality in possession.

He has created 26 chances from open play in La Liga this season, the sixth-highest total across Europe's top five leagues, and wins possession an average of 7.6 times per 90 minutes, the 10th-highest figure.

However, such is Spain's wealth of midfield options that he is not even guaranteed a starting place for his country, with Fabian Ruiz preferred for their final three matches at the 2026 World Cup.

Paris St-Germain midfielder Ruiz, who finished 10th in this year's Ballon d'Or rankings, also deserves to be in any debate about the world's best midfielders.

He might not yet have the profile of Barcelona team-mates Rodri or Pedri, but on current form alone, versatile youngster Lopez is one of Europe's best box-to-box goalscorers.

The 23-year-old already has nine goals and seven assists this season. Counting only goals scored in Europe's top five leagues and the Champions League, no central midfielder has more.

While Lopez can also operate on the wing, the presence of Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon means he has mainly featured as a number eight or a number 10 this term.

The Barcelona academy graduate played only a bit-part role as Spain won Euro 2024 and was unfortunate to miss the World Cup after breaking a bone in his foot in May.

However, a summer off enabled him to hit the ground running this season, and he has not looked back.

#742. What impact will tyre-limit rule have on Qatar GP?

Why a lap limit on tyre usage is again in place at Lusail as we explain, with the help of Bernie Collins, what impact it might have on the weekend; watch every session from the Qatar GP live Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Formula 1 returns to the Middle East this weekend for the first time since pre-season testing in February for back-to-back races to finish the 2026 campaign.

Qatar stages the first of those, with the fast, flowing Lusail International Circuit hosting a Grand Prix for the fifth occasion since its debut in 2021.

As was the case last year, a tyre limit regulation is in place for the race, so what is it and what impact might it have on the weekend?

Pirelli, Formula 1's tyre supplier, last week announced there will be a limit of 27 laps on a set of tyres for this weekend in Qatar.

It is the third time a tyre limit has been implemented for the race at the Lusail International Circuit after punctures at the inaugural 2021 event, and safety concerns being raised during the 2023 weekend.

In 2023, Pirelli mandated a three-stop race and last year they implemented a 25-lap limit which effectively created a two-stop race.

The Qatar Grand Prix is 57 laps so the 27-lap limit for this weekend means, like last year, each driver will need to pit at least twice.

Pirelli explained "the increase [in the limit] has been made possible by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction".

Laps to the grid, formation laps and laps after the chequered flag do not count towards the lap total but laps will be counted cumulatively across all track sessions.

In effect, that means if a driver does three laps on a set of tyres in qualifying, and uses those tyres in the race, they can only do another 24 laps on them before changing in the Grand Prix.

"This precautionary measure is linked to the unique characteristics of the Lusail circuit, which is particularly demanding in terms of energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear," added Pirelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins, a former head of race strategy at Aston Martin, answers several of the key questions around the rule…

Bernie: "Qatar is a very high-speed track and there used to be some very aggressive, sharp-edged kerbs that led to some cuts in the sidewalls of tyres.

"That resulted in quite strong limits on the number of laps in 2023 when an 18-lap tyre limit was imposed.

"That very short limit combined with very hot conditions that year, when the race was held in October, made it very difficult for drivers. They were pushing very hard every lap in very high temperatures, which is one of the reasons why we now declare a heat hazard if it's over 31 degrees and drivers can wear a cooling vest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"Since then, the track has removed some of the harshest edges of the kerbs, which resulted, alongside some cool conditions, teams attempting a one-stop strategy in the 2024 race.

"The difficulty with that was that even though the tyres were now not getting damaged, there was still lots of wear on the tyre because of the high-speed nature of the track. The tyre was wearing down on the surface more than Pirelli were happy with on those one-stop strategies which is why last year we had a 25-lap limit imposed and this year we have 27-lap limit."

How will it change how the teams prepare?

Bernie: "I think teams will have a heads up from Pirelli way before we found out, so they'll have had much longer to prepare for it.

"I think because it's not a Sprint weekend, teams have quite a good allocation of medium or hard tyres in order to do what they need to do. The problem with a Sprint weekend, which Qatar was last year, is that the 25-lap limit also applied through the Sprint itself and Qualifying as it's all cumulative through the weekend.

"So this year, with a normal weekend, and particularly with the medium tyres, the teams have loads available to play with.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"So I'd expect the race to be similar to last year in terms of something like two sets of medium and one set of hard. They will probably still run a hard tyre in Practice Two to try it and then they'll save one for their race allocation. Some teams might save two for the race allocation.

"But I think with it not being a Sprint, the teams should have loads of tyres available to make it happen and it'll just depend on whether they think medium or hard is their preferred tyre for the race."

Bernie: "I don't think the 27-lap limit is very restrictive in terms of strategy because there is lots of freedom with the 57-lap race.

"The earliest you could stop and still do a two-stop race is lap three. So you'd do three laps on one tyre and then one stint of 27 laps followed by another of 27 laps. That strategy might be possible if there's a Safety Car early in the race, meaning you'd have to do one more stop to the end.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"We're not expecting really hot conditions, but not really cold conditions either, so I think the 27-lap limit, depending on when you stop, won't necessarily mean that the drivers can push every single lap. It won't be tyre management and more tyre management because drivers are doing a one-stop, but it won't be pushing every single lap with really short stints like we had in 2023 with the 18-lap limit either. It will be somewhere in between."

Could the rule advantage or disadvantage anyone?

Bernie: "It's hard to say which teams might benefit, or who the rule might hurt, because unlike previous years, we've not had teams really suffering more than others with tyre degradation.

"So I think it's not necessarily going to benefit a lot of teams."

Will teams be wary of avoiding McLaren's 2025 mistake of not pitting under an early Safety Car?

Bernie: "In 2025, the Safety Car came out on lap seven, which was exactly the right lap that you could make it to the end by doing one more stop. McLaren were the only team not to take that and suffered, losing positions as a result.

"This year the lap that can happen is lap three.

"That is very early in the race but because the pit loss in Qatar is so long (26.5s) if the degradation is low enough, which will be driven by track temperature, then you should take the Safety Car stop early on and try to do one stop from there because the saving under the Safety Car is significant compared to the time lost with the pit stop."

Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the Qatar Grand Prix with live coverage from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW

#740. WWE’s Thea Hail Shaves Head on Live TV After Alopecia Diagnosis

WWE NXT star Thea Hail, the mentee of WWE alum Andre Chase, pushed back on the harsh beauty standards for female wrestlers during a Nov. 24 broadcast where she shaved her head.

As the WWE star called out how the sport's fan base puts undue pressure on its female performers "to walk through that curtain and be perfect," she shaved her head in an emotional display in the ring following an alopecia diagnosis in August.

"I'm sure you can all imagine how afraid I was to share with the world that at 23 years old, I was diagnosed with alopecia," Hail tearfully confessed during the Nov. 24 WWE NXT broadcast, "an autoimmune condition that causes you to lose your hair."

And the wrestler admitted that losing 40 percent of her hair in less than four months made her fearful about her future. As she explained, "I'd love to sit here and lie to you guys and tell you that I was super optimistic about this all, but I wasn't."

She noted that her new normal had her especially worried about how she would be judged if her hair never grew back.

"Since July, I've been asking myself the same questions you're all probably wondering," Hail continued. "Most importantly, 'How will other people look at me if I have no hair?'"

As such, her ongoing feud with WWE costar Chantel Monroe, who has frequently used Hail's bald patches as a part of their scripted confrontations on the program, has been difficult for Hail.

"Chantel gave me that answer really quickly, and she proved just about every fear I had to be true," she shared. "She made me feel so small and so defeated as a part of my life that I wasn't ready to share was exposed by somebody else."

In addition, she called out the beauty standard she feels gets held against women in the ring for looking anything from "too muscular" to "too skinny."

"Do you know how long every girl back there sits in the hair and makeup chair before they come out here just so you all don't tear them to shreds?" she questioned. "Because God forbid their extensions don't blend the way that you think they should, or their tan's a little weird, or you don't like their gear."

With that in mind, Hail aimed "to take this moment of weakness and turn it into a strength" to convey how her alopecia has become "a bit of a blessing in disguise."

Ultimately, the Pittsburgh native was all smiles as she ended her heartfelt speech by shaving off her mane with an electric razor while the crowd chanted her name.

Hail first shared her journey with alopecia in an Aug. 27 Instagram, captioned, "i now have alopecia areata… i have literally manifested going bald."

Read on for more stars who have been vulnerable about their health.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus."

"I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor said it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking."

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

"The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months."

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time."

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better."

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much."

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood."

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

"It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'"

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed."

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain."

"It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked."

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

"This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first."

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most."

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian said in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

"'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?"

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert."

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine said in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it."

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an update on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

"There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye."

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment)."

The actress said she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant."

While the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable."

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, New Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent."

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey said the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine."

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I said, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent."

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine."

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that."

#739. China’s AI-powered smart-city model is going global

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Jacob Dreyer is an editor for business, economics, politics and law at Palgrave (a subsidiary of Springer Nature) based in Shanghai, China. The views expressed here are his own.

To understand the Chinese smart city, it helps to know that twenty-first-century infrastructure, technology and policy increasingly makes the whole of China a single, interconnected economic unit. Trains, planes and autonomous vehicles shuttle about, with the centre of megacities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen merely being in the middle of ‘one-hour circles’ for commuters that allow them to reach anywhere in the wider urban area with ease. Previous barriers to the internal movement of workers, such the hukou system, which restricted access to public services based on a person’s birthplace, are being removed, making it easier for people to compete for jobs across the country. And all the while, the Internet supercharges these shifts to a nationwide marketplace, backed by an ever-expanding supply of data centres. Sichuanese farmers of organic lemons now livestream from rural villages on apps such as Xiaohongshu or Douyin as they compete for city restaurateurs to buy their products.

So, if the goal of a ‘smart city’ is to use big data and AI to outsource governance functions, keeping everything running smoothly, then maybe we should think of China as a single city, with its different provinces and megalopolises as neighbourhoods with their own special roles. For instance, three of China’s megacities each have their own important function: Beijing regulates and invests in fundamental research; Shanghai is home to multinational corporations, frontier research in AI and biotech, and finance; and the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen and Guangzhou, is home to innovative manufacturers, such as electric vehicle producer BYD, tech giant Huawei and consumer electronics firm DJI.

China’s 15th five-year plan unveiled earlier this year sees the country in this way, too, by entrusting certain functions to different cities and regions, and with rural areas also playing an essential role. In the northeast, farming is increasingly carried out with the use of drones and big data by state-owned companies such as Beidahuang. In Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang, data centres are powered by abundant solar and wind energy, where they calculate how the self-driving cars of China’s eastern seaboard should navigate roads or process the AI that helps to keep the country’s state-of-the-art high-speed train network running on time.

This approach on data is embodied by 东数西算 (roughly translated as ‘east data, west compute’), a national-level strategic project to channel data from developed eastern regions to resource-rich western regions for processing and storage using eight data-centre ‘hubs’ located across the country. Eastern megacities generate the vast majority of China’s data and AI requests, but they bring skyrocketing land costs, power shortages and cooling difficulties that make hosting data centres unattractive. Instead, the solar farms of Xinjiang’s deserts and the wind farms of the Mongolian steppe are used to provide renewable, cheap energy to data centres.

One key example is Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia, which has been transformed from a traditional farming region into a prominent data powerhouse, earning the name ‘Grassland Cloud Valley’. The energy costs in Ulanqab are low, because the government has been installing massive renewable capacity, relying on the area’s abundant wind and solar resources. Mongolia is cold for most of the year, so data centres use standard air cooling rather than massive air-conditioning set-ups — effectively, they just cover the servers with plastic and leave the door open for wintry winds to circulate. Major firms such as Huawei, Alibaba, Kuaishou and Apple have constructed large-scale cloud bases in Ulanqab. The region houses China’s largest intelligent computing centre for autonomous driving (Fuyao), built by Xpeng Motors and Alibaba Cloud, which has helped make it 170 times faster to train self-driving models. It means an autonomous taxi driving around Beijing is effectively being controlled by servers in the far-away desert of Inner Mongolia.

#738. Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (BIG) campaign called "The King's Return."

BIG, a Christian group for footballers, has said it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

"Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he said.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

"I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone."

He then said that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

In Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp said, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

Klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

#737. Glasner criticises Forest players yet to learn English

Nottingham Forest have suffered successive 2-0 defeats on the road to Brentford and Bournemouth

Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner says standards at the club were not good enough when he arrived, and has questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after being in the country for a number of years.

Forest are one place above the relegation zone heading into Friday's home game against Chelsea, winning just two of their first 11 games in the Premier League.

"Stability in a company is having standards," said Glasner. "Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

"We have players who are here for four years, can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

"For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English. If I want to manage in Italy, I have to speak Italian.

"Otherwise, Oliver Glasner, if you want to speak in your dialect, stay at home in Austria, everybody understands you, but nowhere else."

Forest, who narrowly avoided relegation last season but who did reach the Europa League semi-finals, have had a succession of managers in recent years and while Glasner refused to blame the upheaval for any problems he has inherited, he feels standards need to rise.

"We want to create a stable Nottingham Forest team that can consistently play in the top half of the Premier League," added Glasner, 52.

"We are a few steps away from this but we really believe we know which steps we have to take.

"We are still very ambitious but it looks to take a little bit longer than we all hoped. The goal is getting stability into this club and we're still working on this.

"We knew this is a transition season, let's say like this, where we still stay very ambitious but with a lot of problems to solve."

Glasner held transfer talks with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis in London on Monday as the club prepares their plans for the January transfer window, when they hope to add up to five players to their squad.

"He [Marinakis] was asking 'what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment'," said Glasner.

"He wants the best for Nottingham Forest, he wants the best for everyone here.

"We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling."

#736. Why Ezra Frech's Ear Was Bleeding During DWTS Finale

Dancing With the Stars pro Daniella Karagach explained why her partner Ezra Frech's ear appeared to be bleeding during the Nov. 24 finale before the duo took home the Mirrorball trophy.

Clinching the Mirrorball trophy was music to Ezra Frech’s ears.

Especially since the Paralympian had to power through an ear injury while taking to the dance floor on the season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars Nov. 24.

The 21-year-old raised eyebrows when fans spotted blood on his face after his freestyle performance with partner Daniella Karagach—but it turns out he’d gotten scratched from one of her costumes earlier in the show.

“I’m so freaking sorry,” Karagach exclaimed to Frech in her Nov. 24 Instagram Story. “Are you OK though?”

Frech assured her that he was indeed “fine,” joking that the cuts along his face and his ear were just “battle scars.”

Still, the dance pro was mortified by what her costume had done, exclaiming, “Oh my gosh, your ear. Dude. My dress.”

The track and field star acknowledged that the injury was quite noticeable, adding, “People were like, ‘Your ear was bleeding when you were getting interviewed.’”

Karagach gave her partner one final apology before the duo took to the ballroom for the live finale, waltzing into the history books as Frech became the first amputee and the youngest man to win Dancing With the Stars.

But it wasn’t just a bloody ear Frech was dealing with, as his prosthetic leg accidentally fell off during his freestyle dance to Linkin Park’s “Numb.”

“The leg just wasn't on correctly, and I felt it,” he explained to Variety following the episode. “Sometimes it'll readjust and I'll be OK. And so, as I was running up the steps, I'm like, ‘There's a 50 percent chance my leg will resuction and I'll be OK.’ And that wasn't the case.”

Thanks to the quick thinking of pro Alan Bersten as well as Karagach, Frech was able to take a moment and attach his limb mid-dance before the pair got back in step with the rest of their routine. And Karagach was certainly grateful to have had that moment to reset.

“I was just like, there is no other place in the routine that he can do this right now, and he cannot do the whole routine on one leg,” the 33-year-old explained. “So, I was like, ‘Just put your leg on.’ And it's not like—we had one little trick in there that he did on one, like a 540. It was really impressive. It was really great. But nothing's better than him just clicking on his leg properly and continuing on with the dance. I was like, ‘This is our only shot to do that.’”

The moment definitely left an impression on the audience and the judges, as Derek Hough told the stars, “This performance will have a ripple effect far beyond this show. What you did tonight was forever. Kids will look up to you and see what's possible."

Fellow judge Bruno Tonioli agreed, adding, "What we witnessed tonight goes beyond dancing. This is a powerful, beautiful, life-affirming statement that will inspire the nation and the world."

#735. Regulator chief 'has stomach' to face Man City

Manchester City are currently third in the Premier League

The chair of English football's independent regulator has told MPs he "has the stomach" to take potential action against Manchester City.

The club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-season period by an independent commission.

The verdict, published in September, found City's Abu Dhabi owners - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president Sheikh Mansour - inflated revenues and disguised losses by Â£900 million through "sham" arrangements.

City deny wronging and have appealed, but if the ruling is upheld, they could face an investigation by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

It has the power to remove directors if they are deemed unsuitable, and even to force a sale of the club.

Appearing in front of parliament's Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee, IFR chairman David Kogan was clear that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate the club's hierarchy and take action, if deemed necessary.

"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," he said.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so.

"Would I, with an organisation that has a relatively new, fairly young staff, that's been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not.

"But the truth is, if we don't act - assuming those circumstances are triggered - if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?

"So I think we have to absolutely, clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do, and we absolutely will do that, whatever that means."

De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'

Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue

The fallout from the case has prompted concern that wider UAE investment in UK projects could suffer. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club.

Kogan added: "Does the evidence, if we come to assess it in relation to individuals, stand up in terms of the legislation as being a cause for concern? And if it is, we will have to act appropriately.

"That is the only test, not the politics around it, not the place where it came from, not the size of the club. It is the only test because without that, you cannot have an effective regulator."

When asked how any possible legal battles with City would be paid for, IFR chief executive Richard Monks said a litigation reserve of Â£2m was to be built up over the next two years via a levy charged to the clubs. "When we take litigation, we expect to win and we expect to reclaim costs and repay that reserve from costs," he said.

"Now clearly - and I'm not talking about a specific case - clearly, there could be a very large legal case of any particular club that would require us to spend more than Â£2m in terms of litigation costs and barrister costs in particular. So if that happens, we have agreed with government [that it] will effectively lend us the money in terms of cash flow.

"As I say, we'd expect to win that litigation, to claim costs and repay government. If we failed in that massive litigation, then ultimately it would be added to the levy and we'd repay government that way."

#734. Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed for First Time In History

Ahead of its 100th celebration, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed to Nov. 28 “in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators” due to a severe storm in New York.

If your Turkey Day plans include watching the parade, be prepared for some deflating news.

The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in history, with the milestone 100th celebration being delayed two days until Nov. 28 due to a severe storm headed to New York City, an NBC spokesperson confirmed to E! News.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided,” the spokesperson shared in a Nov. 25 statement, “in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28. More details to follow.”

Macy’s expressed gratitude for the many people who bring the parade to living rooms every Thanksgiving.

“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year,” a spokesperson told MSNOW in a statement. “We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

And while the announcement marks the first time the parade has been postponed since its debut in 1924, the Thanksgiving Day staple has been cancelled three times throughout its 100-year history—from 1942 to 1944—due to World War II.

This year, the monumental centennial celebration was set to take place on Thursday, when a coastal storm is predicted the Big Apple and eastern coastline, bringing rain and strong winds.

This poses a major safety concern not only for the millions of New Yorkers who watch the parade in person, but also for the thousands of performers who participate, alongside the nearly 30 floats and record-breaking 100 inflatables, which will include characters such as Bluey, Buckaroo Bob the Minion and Hello Kitty.

And while viewers at home will have to wait a couple of days to watch the 100th annual Turkey Day spectacular in all of its glory, families will still have some parade entertainment on Thanksgiving.

As an NBC spokesperson shared, the network—which broadcasts the celebration—will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Nov. 26 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.

#733. 'Laughing gas has ended careers' - so how common is it in football?

Watch: Moment Raheem Sterling arrested after car crash

It is known as laughing gas but the impact nitrous oxide can have on a professional footballer's body is anything but funny.

"I'm not going to name names but I have colleagues who know Premier League footballers who are no longer playing as a direct result of nitrous oxide [use]," said Dr David Nicholl.

Nicholl, a clinical lead in neurology with Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, was speaking after former Manchester City, Chelsea, Liverpool and England forward Raheem Sterling was handed a suspended jail term after pleading guilty to dangerous driving.

A key part of the case was that Sterling had been inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon while driving.

His Lamborghini was seen veering across a motorway and later crashed into a metal gate. Sterling, 31, was arrested at the scene and found with six gas canisters in his car.

He disclosed to custody staff "he had a problem with nitrous oxide", the court was told.

Defending Sterling, Jason Bartfeld KC said his client "recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position" and that he has "sought to address" these in the "most positive and effective way and with some success".

So, what is nitrous oxide, how does it affect those who take it and is its use more common in footballers than the wider population?

Footage was released of the footballer driving dangerously

Nitrous oxide's original use was as a sedative that healthcare providers like dentists could use to keep patients comfortable during procedures.

It is now legally sold for catering, medical and industrial purposes, but is frequently used as a recreational drug and is commonly known as laughing gas.

This can be abused by inhaling the gas via a balloon, leading to a short-term high causing symptoms such as brief euphoria, mild perceptual changes and uncontrollable laughter, external.

Nitrous oxide also slows brain and body responses and can displace oxygen in the lungs and bloodstream, contributing to dizziness, confusion or fainting.

It is thought long-term or excessive use can have disastrous effects on the body, from neurological harms to nerve and spinal cord damage which could lead to permanent disability.

According to medical journal The Lancet, it is now the third most commonly used drug after cannabis and cocaine in the UK, with use highest among people aged 16â24 years.

It has been increasing in popularity as a recreational drug over the past decade.

This prompted it to be reclassified as a Class C drug in 2023 after a government consultation.

BBC Sport has been told the abuse of so-called laughing gas has been widespread among professional footballers for a long time.

Former player Drewe Broughton is now a human performance coach, working with Premier League footballers and clubs around the world.

He said laughing gas was seen by some as a release.

"I think the use of nitrous oxide is really common," he added.

"It's something that can be done in private. It's something that can be hidden. You can't smell it on their clothes or the breath. It's an underground thing."

Broughton said he had been in the company of professional players when they had been using 'balloons'.

"I remember sitting in a players' house on the outskirts of Manchester, and these canisters were all over the floor," he added.

"I was from a world where people drank or they gambled or went to pubs and nightclubs. That was my first exposure to it."

Broughton has developed an app to help tackle issues with mental health and under-performance in football.

He said the reasons to use nitrous oxide had always been there: pressure on players to perform leaves them searching for an escape.

But Broughton has concerns about the toll nitrous oxide can take.

"I don't think there's the same awareness around nitrous oxide and damage to the body as there would be around alcohol or other drugs," he said.

BBC Sport has been told that some footballers see laughing gas as an alternative to harder substances because it does not stay in the body's system for more than a few hours.

Luci Hanmer, who works with Lancashire drugs and alcohol support charity 'We Are With You', said a substance like nitrous oxide was hard to detect.

She said: "Anything that you're inhaling, the effects that you're going to feel happen very soon.

"So if you are looking for that escapism, the effects are going to be quick.

"Once ingested, it doesn't last very long within your body compared to some of the other substances which can be detected for quite a number of days.

"So if you're getting a drugs test the next day for example, that won't show up."

Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving

Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha said more support was needed, particularly for players like Sterling who break through young.

Sterling made his debut for Liverpool and England at just 17 - before going on to win four Premier League titles at Manchester City and 82 caps for his country, including the Euro 2020 final at Wembley.

"Look at what's happened to Raheem," he said. "Look at how this led to this moment, a moment which I'm sure he's hugely embarrassed about, because I'm sure he can see how dangerous that was to not just his life, but the lives of so many people who are on the road at the same time.

"But I just don't feel like football is in a position where they think it's important to support people who have issues with nitrous oxide."

The BBC Radio 5 live pundit said the use of nitrous oxide in professional footballing circles was very common.

"I think the difference from when I was younger is that people would openly party in certain places," he said.

"Now they party where they're harder to spot. That's why you don't really see on a week-to-week basis now the scandal of somebody that's been out drinking.

"The players are doing it, but it's more sophisticated in terms of how they do it, the locations, and this is an example here with nitrous oxide."

Neurologist Dr Nicholl has been working with patients who have abused nitrous oxide for years and issued a warning to others.

"It certainly is being used by footballers, but it's pretty much the worst thing that you want to be using if you're a professional sportsperson," he said.

"It damages your spinal cord and the spinal cord is a bit like an electrical cable, where the insulation - the outside of that cable - gets stripped away.

"So what patients will complain of is difficulty with feeling on their hands or feet, or unable to walk at all.

"So, in effect, it's like a spinal cord injury. But they can also get blood clots, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary emboli, and some patients have died."

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line website.

#732. ‘I hope they win Ashes 5-0’ – Stokes backs Root and Fleming's new England

"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at," Stokes told Sky Sports, adding: "I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Former England captain Ben Stokes says he hopes they win next year's Ashes 5-0, though he would not be drawn on Sandpapergate or the possibility of him making a comeback for the series.

Speaking to Sky Sports upon the launch of a new podcast he's presenting with former England team-mate Mark Wood called 'That's Not Cricket', Stokes hinted that he might have more to say on the saga dominating Australian cricket on that platform.

"It would be pretty bizarre for it not to be mentioned [on the podcast]", Stokes said. "It's all kicking off at the moment out there, isn't it?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"What Australia have going on there is far beyond anything we had to deal with [as a leadership group].

"I imagine Joe [Root] and Flem [Stephen Fleming] would be thinking, 'imagine if this happened three weeks before the Ashes next year, as opposed to now'."

England's Test team enter into a new era under Root - who returned to the captaincy with a 3-0 series sweep of Pakistan following Stokes' international retirement - and Fleming, who begins as head coach with a three-Test tour of South Africa next month.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The series, against the reigning World Test Champions, serves as an ideal challenge for the new regime as they steel themselves for the visit of Australia next summer where they'll look to regain the Ashes for the first time since winning on home soil in 2015.

"I'm doing a Glenn McGrath here; I hope England win the Ashes 5-0," Stokes said. "I'm not saying they will, but I wish nothing but the best for them.

"I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well.

"There is no animosity whatsoever between any of us, there's no jealousy."

Stokes did add, however, that he was "surprised" to see Root take on the captaincy again, knowing first-hand how much the job takes out of you - as well as the toll it had taken on Root by the time he handed over the reins in 2022 after five years in the role.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I was a little bit surprised, if I'm being honest, just because he knows what it's like and he's done so well as a player but also, knowing Joe, he feels like he can take the team from where it was and build on it again," Stokes said.

"It's an exciting time for someone to think like that and when Stephen Fleming got appointed, I thought 'these two are going to work really well together'.

"I did a lot of work with Flem in the IPL. He's a great man manager; everyone has already seen how he speaks, which is very impressive. I'm excited to watch them go about it."

Stokes' time as Test captain and as an England cricketer came to an end with a 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand, which was on the heels of a disastrous 4-1 Ashes drubbing in Australia during the winter.

"I was in the right headspace for the Ashes," Stokes reflected. "It was all after that. Before the Ashes, I was so confident.

"Everyone was fit, firing and ready to go. Fans and pundits were all confident, and Australia weren't confident, so we couldn't have been in a better place going out there.

"But emotion and the feeling of what you think is going to happen is completely different to getting out there in the heat of the battle. Everything after that was tough."

Stokes added: "Unfortunately, to do that role, you have to immerse yourself in it, have to throw yourself into it.

"For all the positive stuff that comes with it, there is a negative effect that can flow over into your home life and your family.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I think every England captain will have that. I don't think there is anything you can do.

"You can try your hardest, but when you do that role you just have to do it. I don't think you are doing the role justice if you take it lightly.

"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

As well as still playing for his county side Durham - helping them clinch promotion back to Division One of the County Championship - and an upcoming stint with the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League, Stokes is using his newfound freedom to venture into the world of podcasting.

"I have been in the public eye for so long but people who don't know me probably only know 10, 15, 20 per cent of what I am actually like," he said. "That is the exciting thing: I now get a chance to say what I want to be going out.

"I don't feel like you're always necessarily able to give that full account of yourself as a person, because you're wary of upsetting people. The only person I can upset now is myself.

"It's really exciting and I can't wait to get going. We've got a lot to talk about and a lot to say."
